newsitem.title: CHINA: China to invest $4.1 bln in railway construction.
newsitem.headline: China to invest $4.1 bln in railway construction.

text.p: China plans to invest 34.4 billion yuan ($4.1 billion) in railway construction this year, up from 32 billion yuan in 1996, state media said on Tuesday.

The funds would be used to complete the laying of 1,270 km of track and build 1,260 km of new rail lines, 440 km of double-track rail and 1,750 km of electrified railway, Xinhua news agency and newspapers quoted Railway Minister Han Zhubin as saying.

In 1996, the ministry completed the laying of 1,300 km of track, including 436 km of double-track rail lines, and built 1,980 km of new rail lines, 1,500 km of double-track railways, and nearly 700 km of electrified railways, the reports said.
Han did not say how the money would be raised.

Chinese railway departments attracted overseas investment totalling $370 million in 1996, including $155 million in loans and 184 pieces of equipment purchased with overseas funds, Xinhua said. It gave no comparative figure.
Foreign trade from railway businesses last year totalled $390 million, up 39 percent from 1995, it said.
Foreign contract projects, labour exchanges and designing and consultancy contracts of railway departments totalled $311 million last year, the news agency said.
China's railways handled 942 million passengers and 1,616 million tonnes of cargo in 1996, down 12.3 percent and up 1.4 percent respectively from 1995, newspapers said.
